title: Simple model on a generated idea graph: α × β
html:
Simple model on a generated idea graph: α × β

Question: On a generated idea graph, how far does a society get for the same money, by α and β?

Answer: Best overall: OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value and ROI. (7 measures; a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)

  • hardest level: 5.20 against traditional 0.00, clearly better.
  • targets solved: 0.00 against traditional 0.00, no clear difference.
  • bounty value: 0.00 against traditional 0.00, no clear difference.
  • ROI: 0.00 against traditional 0.00, no clear difference.
  • knowledge found (bits): 106 against traditional 46, clearly better.
  • knowledge per unit of money: 0.09 against traditional 0.04, clearly better.
  • waste: 0.20 against traditional 0.51, clearly better.

Design (fixed before the run): compared α in {1, 0.8, 0.5, 0.2} × β in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} · held the same: a generated idea graph (9 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 4 bits growing by 4 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, budget 1200 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 50 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a generated idea graph (9 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 4 bits growing by 4 per level, composition 0.7); each run draws its own graph. Only α and β vary. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, a budget of 1200 split equally every round (ρ = 0), no mint, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
